docs.title: Home
docs.text:
The Universe of Luau just got simpler.

Comet is a lightweight, portable, component-based framework for Luau. With Comet, you assemble bodies composed of components into hierarchies that are easy to manage, traverse, and extend. Comet helps you write clear, predictable logic that interacts directly with the universe of your codebase. Comet is ready when you are, working in Roblox and beyond.

Get Started! API Refrence

docs.title: API
docs.text: Welcome to the API Refrence! If your new to comet, its recomended to go through the tutorials first. The following Is a list of each cattegory and what they mean:

docs.title: Types
docs.text: information on types. These are often objects that you define.

docs.title: Objects
docs.text: are objects that are defined as part of Comet by default.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: functions that Comet provides.

docs.title: Descendants
docs.text: Returns a list of all Bodys decending the given Body.

docs.title: Destroy
docs.text: Parents a Body and its children to nil and emptys the table, allowing it to garbage collect when all strong refrences are lost.

docs.title: Find
docs.text: Returns a list of all Bodys with the given name decending the given Body.

docs.title: GetChildren
docs.text: Returns a list of all children parented to the given Body.

docs.title: GetComponent
docs.text: Returns a Bodys Component if it has it.

docs.title: GetComponents
docs.text: Returns a list of every Component a Body has.

docs.title: GetParent
docs.text: Returns the parent of the given Body.

docs.title: Parent
docs.text:
Parents a Body to the given Body.

Tip

Its recomended to use the add() function as its more powerful.

docs.title: Universe
docs.text: Creates a new Universe.

docs.title: add
docs.text: Parents a Body or list of Bodys to the given Body.

docs.title: Body
docs.text:
export type Body = {
    Type: "Body",
    Name: string?,
    Parent: Body?,
    _Children: {Body},
    _Universe: Universe,
    Components: {Component}?,
}
An Object made up of Components that makes up the hierarchy data structure.

docs.title: Type: "Body"
docs.text: Identifier used for Comet to recognize the Body.

docs.title: Name: string?
docs.text: Optional name used to uniquely identify the body in errors. Defined through the Name special key.

docs.title: Parent: Body?Future versions of Comet may make this value private!
docs.text:
Refrence to the body this object is parented to.

DO NOT TOUCH THIS!

Do not directly read or set this value as it will cause errors! Use the Parent() and GetParent() method attached to Comet itself.

docs.title: _Children: {Body}
docs.text:
Refrence to the bodys parented to this body.

DO NOT TOUCH THIS!

Do not directly read or set this value as it will cause errors! Use the Parent() and GetChildren() methods attached to Comet itself.

docs.title: _Universe: Universe
docs.text:
A refrence to this Bodys universe.

DO NOT TOUCH THIS!

Do not read or set this value EVER! This is purely for internal use.

docs.title: Components: {Component}?Future versions of Comet may make this value private!
docs.text:
A list of all the components added to the body.

Probably dont touch this

While its safe to use this value. Its recomended to use the GetComponent() and GetComponents() methods attached to Comet itself to increase code clarity.

docs.title: Universe
docs.text:
export type Universe = Body | {
    _Bodys: {Body},
    update: (self: Universe, dt: number) -> (),
    Body: (self: Universe, props: {any}) -> (Body)
}
The root object in the that all Bodys decend from.

docs.title: _Bodys: {Body}
docs.text:
A weak table of all Bodys part of this universe.

Don't use this!

This is used to find all bodys for the update() function, and is not intended for external use!

docs.title: update: (self: Universe, dt: number) -> ()
docs.text: Function thats ran by the user to call the update on all bodys with the given DeltaTime value.

docs.title: Body: (self: Universe, props: {any}) -> (Body)
docs.text: Constructor function that creates Body objects using a list of props. Props can contain Components inside the number keys, and SpecialKeys set to a certain value.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
export type Component = {
    Name: string,
    Init: (Body) -> ()?,
    Start: () -> ()?,
    Update: (dt: number) -> ()?,
    Destroy: () -> ()?,
}
An object passed to a Body to add behavior to them.

docs.title: Name: string
docs.text: A Unique Unique Identifier used for certain helper methods.

docs.title: Init: (Body) -> ()?
docs.text: A function ran which passes the body.

docs.title: Start: () -> ()?
docs.text: A function ran after Init.

docs.title: Update: (dt: number) -> ()?
docs.text: A function ran every frame passing the delta time.

docs.title: Destroy: () -> ()?
docs.text: A function ran before the attached body is destroyed.

docs.title: SpecialKey
docs.text:
export type SpecialKey = {
    Type: "SpecialKey",
    Stage: "PreComponents" | "InitComponents" | "PostComponents",
    Name: string?,
    Method: (Body, any) -> (),
}

Note

I am aware the syntax highlighting is broken, I am not aware how to fix it.

A object passed as a key when creating a Body used to add extra data.

docs.title: Type: "SpecialKey"
docs.text: An Identifier used for Comet to recognise that you passed a SpecialKey.

docs.title: Stage: "PreComponents" | "InitComponents" | "PostComponents"
docs.text: What stage of object creation the body uses.

docs.title: "PreComponents"
docs.text: Before a component init function is ran

docs.title: "InitComponents"
docs.text: After a components init function is ran and before the start function.

docs.title: "PostComponents"
docs.text: After Components init and start function have been run.

docs.title: Name: string?
docs.text: An identifier used in things like errors.

docs.title: Method: (Body, any) -> ()
docs.text: The function that is ran by the body. The body is the body object created, the any is the value the special key was set too.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
Welcome to the tutorials! Here you will learn how to use Comet! Before you get started its expected you know the following subjects:

  • Luau - This is not a luau tutorial! You should understand how to use it.

Here's Some advice:

Please remember that Comet is by design, an incredibly simple and lightweight framework. It doesn't do a lot for you, It provides the basics and expects you to build off of it for your project. For example, Comet comes with no components out of the box

Comet2D

Comet2D is another work-in-progress engine built by Judash399 (The same developer as Comet!). If your looking for a 2D engine that handles more for you while still using Comet as a base, check out Comet2D

docs.title: Comet is in a pre-release state!
docs.text:
This means that Comet is not finalized. Breaking changes are possible between updates that can fundamentally change the way Comet is used.

Updates may break past code, and backwards combatiblity is not guranteed!

We hope you enjoy using Comet!

docs.title: Bodys
docs.text:
Bodys are the object that a Universe itself is made of. Bodys is a data object that is made up of components. You can create new bodys by calling the Body() method on a Universe. This function takes a table like so: 

local body = Universe:Body({})
Technacly though, in Luau if your passing a single string, or table into a function you don't need the parantheses meaning that these mean the same thing: 
--This
local body = Universe:Body({})
--Is the same as
local body = Universe:Body {}
This is the recomended way to create Bodys in Comet and you will see it throughout the rest of the tutorials.

docs.title: Parents
docs.text:
Parenting allows you to control how an object behaves with other objects. By default, a body will not be parented to anything, this is why Comet goes with an add() method, which takes an input of the parent and the child. 

--You can parent a body to the universe
Comet.add(Universe, {
    Universe:Body {}
})

--Or other bodys
Comet.add(otherBody, {
    Universe:Body {}
})
You could also use the Comet.Parent() method to parent a single child, but its recomended to only use Comet.add() as its more powerful.

Abstract

The reason you are able to Parent a body to the Universe is because it is also is a Body object, meaning pretty much all methods that work on bodys will work on the Universe.

docs.title: Destruction
docs.text:
Whenever your done with a Body you can use the Destroy() function attached to Comet to destroy it. 

Comet.Destroy(body)
This will destroy the Body and all of its decendents.

docs.title: Managing the Hierarchy
docs.text: Comet goes with many functions to help you manage the Body hierarchy. Below are some commonly used ones.

docs.title: add()
docs.text:
As already discussed, add() lets you parent a list of bodys to another body. 

Comet.add(body, {
    body1,
    body2,
    body3
})

docs.title: Decendents()
docs.text:
Allows you to get the decendents of an body. 

local decendents = Comet.Decendents(body)

docs.title: Find()
docs.text:
Allows you to find decendents of an object under a certain name defined by the Name special key. 

local fooBodys = Comet.Find(body, "Foo")

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: To install Comet please use one of the following methods.

docs.title: Releases, For standalone projects
docs.text: Go to the Github releases page, and download the comet.luau file from the latest release. Place it into your project. Then require the file in your main script.

docs.title: Releases, Roblox
docs.text: Go to the Github releases page, and download the comet.luau file from the latest release. Then, drag and drop it into your place. Then require it.

docs.title: Wally, Roblox
docs.text:
Add this line into your wally dependencys, and re-run wally install to install Comet 

comet = "judash399/comet@0.1.0"

docs.title: SpecialKeys
docs.text:
SpecialKeys allow you to declaratively configure a Body at creation time by adding new data. They are especially helpful when creating custom engine features such as Tags.

How do they work?

SpecialKeys work by using a table as a unique key in the body creation table. This naturally means that there cannot be SpecialKey duplicates because you cannot have a key equal 2 values.

Comet By default includes 2 default special keys.

docs.title: Name
docs.text:
You can use the Name special key to give a name identifier to an object: 

local player = Universe:Body {
    [Comet.Name] = "Player"
}

docs.title: Children
docs.text:
You can use the Children special key to parent a list of Bodies to the body being created. 

local player = Universe:Body {
    [Comet.Children] = {
        Universe:Body {}
    }
}

docs.title: Defining your own SpecialKeys
docs.text:
The real power of special keys comes when you define your own. You can define one like this: 

local TestKey = {
    Type = "SpecialKey",
    Stage = "PreComponents",
    Name = "TestKey",
    Method = function(body, value)
        print(value)
    end,
}
The Stage field defines what Stage the Key will run at, there are 3 stages:

  • PreComponents - Runs before any components are created. Use for structural setup.
  • InitComponents - Runs after all components exist and their Init() methods have run.
  • PostComponents - Runs after the body is fully constructed and ready for use.

To learn more about defining special keys, check out the tag project.

docs.title: Universes
docs.text:
Universes are the game world for your scene. Its the root body that contains all other bodys. Universes can be created by calling the Universe() method on the Comet table. 

local Universe = Comet.Universe()

docs.title: Projects
docs.text:
Projects are tutorials that focus on teaching you how to implement custom features in Comet. Each project highlights a specific aspect of the engine and shows how to extend it.

Because Comet is intentionally minimal, most of its power comes from adding your own behavior. Feel free to jump to any project that sparks your interest!
